Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
It looks like a fairly straight forward Gangrel deck, with a couple of
Nosferatu in for spice. It looks like it will have trouble working, as it
doesn't have that much intercept, it has no way to make bleeds big (and
thus inspire your prey to block), and it can't get into fights directly

(no Bum Rush or Haven Uncovered). Because of the lack of OBF in the deck,

you would be better off to lose the Nosferatu all together, except for
Ebanezzer Roush and Daliyah, and then double up on Zack North and Badger
in the crypt. My advice:

-Loose the 6 Obf cards and replace them with either Earth Control (+1/+2

stealth) or Form of Mist (S:CE continue action at +1 stealth).

-Lose the Nosferatu as discribed above (And I'm the one who loves the
Nosferatu).

-Add some sort of direct attack abilities. No one is going to block your
bleeds, as you are only going to bleed for one, and if they do block you,
you will kill them, so they won't. With only 7 cards in an 80 card deck
to provide intercept, you won't be able to intercept all that much either.

-Try to con all of your fellow players out of their Immortal Grapples.

This is the most important card you can get for a Pot combat deck, as it
makes you immune to S:CE (Strike: Combat Ends, like Majesty or Earth
Meld), your opponents can't Dodge you, and they can't use guns against
you. With Immortal Grapple, your deck will become an absolute terror
(especially if you are the only one using Fortitude). Just convince your
friends that they are useless, and then trade them good stuff for them.
Then make all their vamps dissapear in a hail of 5 point aggro hits.

-Add some manuvers like Fake Outs and Form of the Ghost. Without

manuvers, a hand damage deck is useless against any deck with guns or
manuvers ("Boy, you certainly do have 5 aggro hand damage, WAY over there.
I guess I'll stay over by this deli...").

-While I am always a fan of the Garou, they very often just end up costing

you 5 pool, and get killed by another combat deck. In a game filled with
Malkavians and Toreadors, the Garou will eat well, but vs the Gangrel,
Nosferatu and Brujah, they will just end up dead.

It looks like a basis for a good Pot/Pro "Burn'em Up" deck, but it needs

some focus to make the combat work well. Trying to get the Edge and
keeping it depends too much on the strength of the other players to avoid
being bled, so that is a crap shoot at best.

I had a good Nosferatu (with a couple of Gangrel) Pot/Pro deck that would

regularly vaporize a couple of vamps a game for a while, but it was SO
card intensive that it was very hard to make it work. For maximum effect,
I needed to have in my hand (or manage to draw):

Bums Rush (to get in combat with the victim of choice)
Some stealth card (to not get blocked)
An extra manuver card (just in case)
Immortal Grapple (Because it is the linch pin in the plan)
Torn Signpost (for 3 hand damage)
Undead Strength (total 5 hand damage)
Claws of the Dead (poof)

This would make a vamp with 3 or less blood vanish (we use the Jyhad aggro

rules), as long as they didn't accidentally have Fortitude cards. It
happened occasionally, and was fun when it did, but was only a sure thing
against the (pre Thoughts Betrayed) Malkavians, anyone I know who wasn't
using Fortitude. A very difficult thing to make work.

Good Luck,

-Peter D Bakija

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
Yah, the VTES aggro rules are different from the Jyhad aggro rules. In
Jyhad, the first point of aggro damage a vamp takes does not cause any
blood loss, it just sends the vamp to torpor. Any extra aggro damage
removes blood, but the first point from a strike does not, so if a vamp
takes 3 aggro damage, they only lose 2 blood. If a vamp has no blood when
they take a point of aggro, they just go to torpor, rather than being
burned, like in VTES. Thus, to burn a vamp using Jyhad rules, you need to
do X+2 aggro damage, where X is the vamps current blood level, as the
first point will send them to torpor, and the rest will burn them.

This is one of the main big differences between Jyhad and VTES, as in VTES
cards like Pulled Fangs and the Ivory Bow become very powerful burning
agents, where in Jyhad, they would just send you to torpor. The Ivory Bow
in Jyhad could never burn anyone, as it could only do 1 aggro. The same
with Pulled Fangs. In VTES, either of these cards will burn a vamp with
zero blood, which makes them much more powerful than they used to be.

Yes, that "Pot/Pro" aggro deck I had described had plenty of problems,

most of which stemmed from, as you pointed out, having no way to avoid
damage. Thus, I played it a couple of times and got a special little
thrill by vaporizing 2 or 3 vamps a game, even though I lost all the time.

As I feel it is my mission in life to make a good Nosferatu deck, I took
it apart and put together my "It only works if I get out Marty Lechtansi"
deck. It is a kind of brutal Pot/For combat deck, with some stealth for
unblockable rushes and bleeding, and some Dom for Conditioning and
Deflections. It works ok, but only if I get out Marty Lechtansi (thus,
the name...) :-)

-Peter D Bakija

>>

>>cards like Pulled Fangs and the Ivory Bow become very powerful burning
>>agents, where in Jyhad, they would just send you to torpor. The Ivory Bow
>>in Jyhad could never burn anyone, as it could only do 1 aggro. The same
>>with Pulled Fangs. In VTES, either of these cards will burn a vamp with
>>zero blood, which makes them much more powerful than they used to be.

>Hmmm. I suppose they tried to make aggravated damage more powerfull

>considering the strange ruling on Rotschreck? We play Jyhad aggro, and
>just ignore Rotschreck.

The aggro rules were changed to simplify them, and to prevent some
non-sensical effects.

In Jyhad, when multiple batches of agg are done, each batch after the
first 'wastes' a point of agg damage by re-sending the target to torpor.
It wasn't always clear what constituted a separate batch.

Also, someone with aggravated damage fighting an Undeadly Persistent vampire
would do less damage than someone with normal damage (e.g., every punch
from Basilia would have no effect, whereas every punch from Nik would
cause a blood to be burned).

In VtES, it doesn't matter how you lump or separate the agg damage (so
long as you apply non-agg before agg) - the net result is always exactly
the same. As an added bonus, agg damage is never inferior to normal.
--
